title: Lipid metabolism-related genes regulate the immune microenvironment during ex vivo lung perfusion for lung transplants
summary: Analysis of donor-lung transcriptomes before and after ex-vivo lung perfusion identified UGCG, SAMD8 and MED26 as upregulated lipid-metabolism genes associated with natural-killer-cell states. Biomarker AUCs were 0.986 in GSE127057 and 0.922 in the independent GSE127055 cohort; a mouse EVLP model reproduced increased expression of all three genes. Expression and immune-cell associations do not establish causal regulation or clinical utility.
ai_technology: WGCNA with LASSO, random forest and XGBoost feature analysis
organization: Department of Thoracic Surgery and Oncology, The First Affiliated Hospital of Guangzhou Medical University, China State Key Laboratory of Respiratory Disease & National Clinical Research Center for Respiratory Disease, Guangzhou, China; Department of Thoracic Surgery, The First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, Zhengzhou University, Zhengzhou, China; Division of Hypertension and Vascular Diseases, Department of Cardiology, Heart Center, The First Affiliated Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University, Guangzhou, China

evidence.tested: WGCNA and LASSO, random forest and XGBoost prioritized genes in GSE127057; GSE127055 provided independent cohort validation. Murine EVLP experiments assessed gene expression and reproduced upregulation of UGCG, SAMD8 and MED26.
evidence.unknown: Gene-expression and immune-cell correlations do not establish causal regulation; clinical monitoring or treatment benefit was not tested.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning feature selection prioritized lipid-metabolism genes in donor-lung expression data; separate murine EVLP experiments checked expression changes.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
